epic.intent:
Dark Mechanicus plans and tracks the work agents do, but the agents live elsewhere: a person installs Claude Code, Codex or Cursor by hand and wires it up over MCP. This epic brings the three big agent CLIs into the desktop app, so a person can connect them in a couple of clicks and talk to them per folder with that folder's Dark Mechanicus tools already wired in.

**What changes**
- **Agents category.** A new **AGENTS** section sits above **FOLDERS** in the sidebar. Its **+** replaces the main pane (folder home or plan graph) with three cards: Claude (Claude Code CLI, `claude`), Codex (Codex CLI, `codex`) and Cursor (Cursor CLI, `agent`, formerly `cursor-agent`). Each card has **Find** (point at an installed executable) and **Download** (install it from the vendor's official source and hook it up). Connected agents are listed in the section, and clicking one opens its page.
- **Agents block per folder.** Every initialized folder gets an **Agents** block under its epic buckets listing that folder's chats. A new chat asks for the agent, then the model, then the Dark Mechanicus role. It runs in that folder, keeps its transcript and the agent's context across restarts, and can switch model between turns. The agent is fixed for the life of the chat.
- **Ask each time.** Before the agent edits a file or runs a command, the chat shows an approval request (Allow once, Allow for this chat, Deny). Nothing happens until the person answers.
- **Start run picks an orchestrator.** **Start run** opens a dialog: run the epic with a connected agent and model (Dark Mechanicus queues the run and starts an orchestrator chat for it), or leave the run pending for an external orchestrator, as today.

**Decisions (from the person, 2026-10-03)**
- CLIs only. The GUI apps (Cursor IDE, Claude Desktop, Codex app) are out of scope.
- Chat history is app-wide: stored in the app's user data, keyed by folder, never in the repository.
- Each chat gets this folder's Dark Mechanicus MCP server with a role picked per chat.
- Approvals are asked each time, in the chat.
- The agent is fixed per chat; the model can change between turns.

**Integration surface per CLI** (checked 2026-10-03; re-check vendor docs while building)
- Claude: the Claude Agent SDK driving the user's `claude` binary (`pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`), `canUseTool` for approvals, `resume` for context, `mcpServers` for Dark Mechanicus.
- Codex: `codex app-server` (JSON-RPC over stdio): `thread/start`, `thread/resume`, `turn/start` with a per-turn model, `model/list`, and the command and file-change approval requests.
- Cursor: `agent acp` (Agent Client Protocol over stdio): `session/new` with `mcpServers`, `session/load`, `session/request_permission`, and `agent models` for the model list.

**Product-plan change.** `docs/product-plan.md` says the agent host does spawning and model selection and keeps vendor names out of plans. This epic makes the desktop app an agent host for these three CLIs. Vendor specifics stay inside per-agent adapters in the main process; plan, ticket and profile schemas stay provider-neutral.

**Out of scope**
- The GUI apps, switching agent within a chat, and committing chat history to Git.
- Collecting or storing vendor credentials: sign-in always goes through the CLI's own login.
- Live activity views of workers and the orchestrator (the separate "Live agent activity" epic builds on this one).

successCriteria.text: The sidebar shows an AGENTS section above FOLDERS; pressing its + replaces the main pane with Claude, Codex and Cursor cards, each with Find and Download.

Find connects a picked executable only after it runs and identifies itself as that agent; Download installs the CLI from the vendor's official source after the person confirms and then shows it connected with its version, on Windows and macOS.
Each initialized folder shows an Agents block; creating a chat there asks for agent, then model, then Dark Mechanicus role, and the chat runs in that folder.
A chat keeps its transcript and the agent's context across closing and reopening the app; the model can be changed between turns and the agent cannot.
Before the agent edits a file or runs a command, the chat shows an approval request; the action happens only after Allow, and Deny is reported back to the agent, for all three agents.
A chat's agent can call this folder's Dark Mechanicus tools with the role chosen for the chat, and the chat appears as a session in the app.
The app never asks for or stores vendor passwords, API keys or tokens; sign-in uses each CLI's own login.
Start run asks whether to run the epic with a connected agent and model, which then orchestrates in a new chat, or to leave the run pending for an external orchestrator to pick up.

epic.title: Agents: connect Claude, Codex and Cursor and chat with them per folder

bundle.rationale:
**Sprint shape.** Sprint 1 is usable on its own: agents can be connected and signed in. Sprint 2 builds the runtime behind a fake adapter first, then the three adapters in parallel. Sprint 3 puts the UI on top, then docs, then an end-to-end check on both platforms.

**Assumptions made while planning (confirm or change)**
- Reads and searches inside the folder run without a prompt; file edits, commands and other side effects ask.
- Planner and orchestrator chats created by hand default to Allow save on, matching **Connect Claude Code**. Orchestrators launched by Start run have it off, since running a saved plan never saves one.
- The Start run choice was added by the person on 2026-10-03 while this plan was being drafted.
- Untracking a folder keeps its chats; tracking it again shows them.
- Download keeps each vendor installer's default location, so the terminal and the app share one binary; binary-only releases go into an app-managed folder.
- No epic branch was named. Set one before starting a run.
- Vendor protocol details (SDK options, app-server and ACP methods, installer URLs) were checked on 2026-10-03 and must be re-checked while building.
- Ticket sizes are written in each body because this server version has no size field yet.

exitCriteria.text: On Windows and macOS, each of the three agents can be connected with Find or Download and shows its version and sign-in state in the AGENTS section.
The + next to AGENTS replaces the main pane with the three agent cards, and the main process never runs an executable path the renderer supplied.

sprints.goal: Connect agents: a person can find or install the Claude, Codex and Cursor CLIs, sign in, and see them in the AGENTS section.

exitCriteria.text: Through IPC, a chat with each agent streams a reply, is stored, resumes with its context after a restart, and switches model between turns (adapter tests replay recorded sessions).
Every file edit or command each agent attempts arrives as an approval request and runs only after Allow.

sprints.goal: Chat runtime: the main process runs a chat with any of the three agents in a folder, stores it, resumes it, and routes approvals.

exitCriteria.text: From a folder's Agents block a person creates a chat (agent, model, role), converses, approves or denies actions, switches model, stops a turn, and finds the chat again after restarting the app, on Windows and macOS.
Start run can launch a connected agent as the run's orchestrator in a new chat, or leave the run pending for an external orchestrator.
The product plan, architecture doc and an agents runbook describe the feature.

sprints.goal: Chat in the app: a person creates, reads and drives chats from each folder's Agents block, and the feature is documented and verified on both platforms.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `list` returns an empty list when `agents.json` is missing or unreadable, and a corrupt file is left in place until the next successful write.
`upsert` keeps one entry per kind, and every write goes through a temp file and a rename (asserted through the injected filesystem).
`remove` drops only that kind's entry and never touches the executable.
Unit tests in `src/main/desktop/agentRegistry.test.ts` were written first, failed for the right reason, and pass; `npm run typecheck` passes.

tickets.body:
Size: **small**.

Add a machine-local registry of connected agents in the main process, stored at `userData/agents.json`. Follow the pattern of `src/main/desktop/folderRegistry.ts`: an injectable filesystem surface, atomic writes (temp file then rename), and a zod-validated read that tolerates a missing or corrupt file.

**In scope**
- Agent kinds are a closed set: `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, each with a display name and the executable names it expects (`claude`, `codex`, `agent` or `cursor-agent`; `.exe` or `.cmd` on Windows).
- An entry records kind, executable path, version (as last probed), how it was connected (`found` or `downloaded`) and timestamps. One entry per kind.
- Operations: `list`, `upsert` (replace the entry for a kind), `remove` (the registry entry only; never uninstalls the CLI).
- Shared view types (`AgentKind`, `AgentView`) in `src/shared/desktop/api.ts`.

**Out of scope:** probing, installing, IPC and UI (later tickets).

**Verify:** unit tests with an injected filesystem.

reasoning.rationale: A small registry module that mirrors an existing pattern.

tickets.title: Add the app-wide agent registry

acceptanceCriteria.text: Picking an executable whose version output identifies the expected CLI stores it with the probed version; a different program, a non-executable file, or one that runs past the timeout is refused with a specific reason and stores nothing.
On Windows a `.cmd` shim is probed without passing unescaped user-controlled text to a shell (unit test with a path containing spaces and `&`).
No IPC channel accepts an executable path from the renderer (test asserts the channel input schemas).
Probe and IPC handler tests were written first and pass with a fake process runner; `npm run typecheck` passes.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**Find** lets a person point Dark Mechanicus at an agent CLI they already have.

**In scope**
- Main opens a native file dialog for the kind (filtered to plausible executable names per OS) and probes the pick by running it with its version flag (`claude --version`, `codex --version`, `agent --version`), with a short timeout and no shell. The output must identify the expected CLI. Anything else is refused with a specific reason ("This is not the Codex CLI", "It did not start", "It timed out").
- Windows: npm-style installs are `.cmd` shims, and Node refuses to spawn `.cmd` files without a shell. Resolve the shim to its underlying script, or run it through `cmd.exe` with arguments that cannot be injected. Never pass user-controlled text through a shell.
- On success, upsert the registry entry (connected via `found`).
- IPC: narrow typed channels `agents:list`, `agents:find` and `agents:remove` through `src/main/desktop/ipc.ts`, `handlers.ts`, `src/preload/index.ts` and `DmApi` in `src/shared/desktop/api.ts`, guarded like the existing channels (`src/main/ipcGuard.ts`).
- **Security:** the renderer never sends a path to execute. Executables come only from the main-process dialog, the installer (next ticket) or the registry. The Electron baseline (contextIsolation, sandbox) is unchanged.

**Out of scope:** Download, sign-in, UI.

**Verify:** unit tests with a fake process runner and dialog.

reasoning.rationale: Process spawning across Windows and macOS with an IPC security boundary.

tickets.title: Find an agent: verify a picked executable and connect it

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each kind has an install recipe for Windows and macOS whose sources are vendor-official HTTPS endpoints, each with a link to the vendor doc it came from; the renderer can pass only the kind (test asserts the channel input).
No network request and no process starts before the person confirms (test with fake fetch and runner).
A checksum mismatch or a failing installer leaves the registry unchanged and reports the reason and the installer's last output lines.
A successful install is probed and stored with its version, and running Download again on an installed agent updates the stored version.
Tests were written first and pass with fake download and process runners; no test touches the network.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**Download** installs the CLI and connects it with no further steps.

**In scope**
- One install recipe per kind and platform (Windows x64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x64), using only the vendor's official source over HTTPS:
  - Claude: Anthropic's native installer (`https://claude.ai/install.ps1` on Windows, `https://claude.ai/install.sh` on macOS).
  - Codex: OpenAI's official release for the platform (`openai/codex` GitHub releases, or the vendor's installer if one exists by then).
  - Cursor: Cursor's installer (`https://cursor.com/install?win32=true` through PowerShell on Windows, `https://cursor.com/install` on macOS).
  Confirm each source against the vendor's current docs while building, and record the docs link next to each recipe.
- Before anything runs, the app shows a confirmation with the source URL, what will run and where it installs. Nothing downloads until the person confirms.
- Verify a published checksum or signature when the vendor provides one, and refuse on mismatch. Vendor installers keep their default location, so the terminal and the app use the same binary. A binary-only release goes into an app-managed folder under `userData/agents/<kind>/`.
- Stream progress (phase, and percent where known) to the renderer. A failure leaves no half-registered agent and reports the installer's last output lines.
- After install, locate the executable, probe it with the probe from the Find ticket, and upsert the registry entry (connected via `downloaded`). Running Download again updates an installed agent.
- IPC: `agents:download` takes the kind only, never a URL or path, plus a progress event.

**Out of scope:** sign-in (separate ticket), Linux.

**Verify:** unit tests with fake download and process runners. No test touches the network.

reasoning.rationale: Downloads and runs vendor installers on two platforms; must be safe, confirmable and verifiable.

tickets.title: Download an agent: install each CLI from its official source

tickets.body:
Size: **small**.

A connected agent is only usable once its CLI is signed in.

**In scope**
- Detect sign-in state per kind with the CLI's own status command (for example `codex login status`, `agent status`, and Claude Code's auth status command), with a timeout. Report `signed_in`, `signed_out` or `unknown` with the reason.

- The app never shows a password or API key field, and never reads or stores credentials or tokens.
- IPC: `agents:status` and `agents:signIn`, taking the kind only.

**Verify:** unit tests with recorded status outputs for each CLI.

reasoning.rationale: Maps three CLIs' status outputs and launches their login commands.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Contract types and a zod schema for stored items exist; an item of unknown kind fails validation without breaking the rest of the chat.
Creating, appending to, listing and reopening a chat round-trips through the store, and a truncated final line is skipped on read (unit tests with an injected filesystem).
Chats are keyed by canonical folder path, so two spellings of the same folder find the same chats, and untracking a folder does not delete them.
A claim token in any item text or tool input is masked before it is stored or emitted (unit test with a real token shape).
Tests were written first and pass; `npm run typecheck` passes.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

The provider-neutral shape every adapter and the UI share, and where chats live.

**Contract** (`src/shared/agents/chat.ts`)
- A chat has an id, folder (canonical path), agent kind, current model, Dark Mechanicus role and allow-save flag, title, timestamps, and the vendor session id.
- A transcript is an ordered list of items: user message, assistant text (streamed as deltas, stored whole), tool call (name, summarized input, status, result summary), approval request and its decision, model change, error, and a context-reset notice.
- An adapter interface (`start`, `send`, `setModel`, `stop`, `listModels`, `dispose`) emits these items and approval requests.
- Leave room for nested threads (a `threadId` on items) so subagent threads can be added later without migrating stored chats.

**Store** (main)
- `userData/agents/chats/<folder key>/<chat id>.jsonl` plus an index per folder, keyed by the same canonical path as the folder registry.
- Append-only writes. Reads tolerate a truncated last line.
- Chats stay when a folder is untracked, and show again when it is tracked again.

**Secrets.** Before an item is written or sent to the renderer, mask anything shaped like a Dark Mechanicus claim token (`<attempt id>.<secret>`, see `src/core/services/attempts.ts`). Orchestrator chats pass execution packets, which carry tokens, to their workers.

**Out of scope:** process management and vendor adapters.

reasoning.rationale: A shared contract three adapters and the UI depend on, plus durable storage and secret masking.

tickets.title: Define the chat contract and the app-wide chat store

acceptanceCriteria.text: With a fake adapter, a chat created through IPC streams items to the renderer channel and to the store, in order.

An approval request blocks the fake adapter until answered; Allow once, Allow for this chat and Deny reach the adapter as distinct outcomes; an unanswered request is still pending after the chat is reopened.
The adapter receives a Dark Mechanicus server entry with the chat's role and label, and `--allow-save` only for planner or orchestrator chats that allow it.
Stop ends the running turn, and quitting the app disposes every adapter process (test asserts dispose is called on all).
Tests were written first and pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**In scope**
- A session manager in main owns one adapter process per active chat. It starts the process on first send (or on open when the vendor needs it), runs it with the folder as working directory, stops the running turn on **Stop**, disposes idle processes, and kills all child processes when the app quits (no orphans on Windows or macOS).
- **Dark Mechanicus MCP per chat.** Build the server entry with `buildMcpConfig` (`src/main/desktop/mcpConfig.ts`) plus `--role <chat role>`, `--allow-save` when the chat allows it (planner and orchestrator only; on by default, like **Connect Claude Code**), and `--label "<Agent> · <chat title>"`, and pass it to the adapter. The chat then shows up as a session in the app.
- **Approvals.** Adapters raise requests (kind: file edit, command or other; a summary; the raw detail). The manager queues them per chat, stores them as transcript items, and blocks the adapter until the person answers Allow once, Allow for this chat, or Deny. A pending request survives the window closing and can be answered when the chat is opened again. Reads and searches inside the folder do not ask.
- **Model.** `setModel` applies from the next turn and records a model-change item.
- **IPC:** `chats:list(folder)`, `chats:create`, `chats:open`, `chats:send`, `chats:stop`, `chats:setModel`, `chats:answerApproval`, `chats:models(kind)`, and a push channel for transcript items and approval requests. All are typed in `DmApi` and guarded.

**Verify:** tests with a fake adapter. The real adapters are the next three tickets.

reasoning.rationale: Child-process lifecycle, a blocking approval queue and concurrency across chats; errors here leak processes or run unapproved actions.

tickets.title: Run chats in the main process: session manager, approvals queue and IPC

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recorded session replays into the expected transcript items (assistant text, tool call, tool result).
Edit, Write and Bash requests become approval requests and run only on Allow; Read, Glob and Grep inside the folder do not ask.
Reopening a chat passes the stored session id to resume; a failed resume yields a context-reset item and a new session.
The model list and a per-turn model change are covered by tests, and the Dark Mechanicus server is passed in `mcpServers`.
Tests were written first and pass; `npm run build` passes with the SDK bundled.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**In scope**
- Drive the connected `claude` executable through the Claude Agent SDK for TypeScript (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` from the registry), in the folder, with streaming input so one process carries several turns.
- **Approvals.** `canUseTool` turns each file edit and command (Edit, Write, Bash and other side-effecting tools) into an approval request. Read and search tools inside the folder are allowed without asking. Allow for this chat allows that tool for the rest of the session.
- **Context.** Store the SDK session id; reopening a chat resumes it (`resume`). If the session cannot be resumed (deleted on disk, CLI reinstalled), record a context-reset item and continue in a new session.
- **Models.** List from the SDK where it exposes supported models, otherwise a curated list with free entry. `setModel` applies from the next turn.
- Pass the Dark Mechanicus server through `mcpServers`.
- Map SDK messages to contract items.
- Add the SDK dependency, check its licence, and make sure it bundles into the main-process build (`electron.vite.config.ts`).

**Verify:** tests replay recorded SDK message sequences. No test calls the network or needs a signed-in CLI.

reasoning.rationale: Maps a vendor SDK's streaming and permission model onto the shared contract.

tickets.title: Add the Claude adapter on the Agent SDK and the user's claude binary

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recorded exchange replays into the expected transcript items.
Command and file-change approval requests become approval requests, and the three decisions map to the protocol's approve-once, approve-for-session and decline.
Resume uses the stored thread id; a failed resume yields a context-reset item and a new thread.
`model/list` feeds the model list, a model change applies on the next `turn/start`, and the user's Codex config file is never written (test asserts).
Tests were written first and pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**In scope**
- Run `codex app-server` from the registry's path in the folder and speak its JSON-RPC over stdio: `initialize`, `thread/start` (or `thread/resume` with the stored thread id), `turn/start` with the input and the chat's model, and `turn/interrupt` for Stop.
- **Approvals.** Answer the command-execution and file-change approval requests with the person's decision (approve once, approve for session, decline). Pick an approval policy and sandbox that make every file change and command ask while reads proceed, and document the choice in the adapter.
- **Models.** `model/list` feeds the list; the per-turn model goes on `turn/start`.
- **Dark Mechanicus server.** Pass it as an MCP server for this process only (config override flags or thread config). Never edit the user's `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- Context reset handling as in the Claude adapter.

**Verify:** tests replay recorded JSON-RPC exchanges.

reasoning.rationale: Implements a JSON-RPC client for a vendor protocol, including approvals and resume.

tickets.title: Add the Codex adapter on codex app-server

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recorded exchange replays into the expected transcript items.
Every `session/request_permission` becomes an approval request and is always answered; the three decisions map to allow-once, allow-always and reject-once.
Resume uses `session/load` with the stored session id; a failed load yields a context-reset item and a new session.
The model list comes from the CLI, and a model change applies on the next turn.
Tests were written first and pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**In scope**
- Run `agent acp` (Agent Client Protocol, JSON-RPC over stdio) from the registry's path in the folder: `initialize`, `session/new` with the folder and the Dark Mechanicus server in `mcpServers`, `session/load` to resume, `session/prompt` for a turn, and `session/cancel` for Stop.
- **Approvals.** Answer `session/request_permission` with the person's decision (`allow-once`, `allow-always`, `reject-once`). Always answer: an unanswered request blocks the tool.
- **Models.** List with `agent models` (or `--list-models`). Apply a model change from the next turn through the protocol if it supports it, otherwise restart the process with `--model` and `session/load`.
- Cursor staff said in March 2026 that `--approve-mcps` is not wired into ACP. Check whether the Dark Mechanicus server needs enabling (`agent mcp enable`) and handle it without touching unrelated user config.
- Context reset handling as in the other adapters.

**Verify:** tests replay recorded ACP exchanges.

reasoning.rationale: Implements an ACP client for a vendor CLI, including permissions, resume and model switching.

tickets.title: Add the Cursor adapter on agent acp

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**In scope**

acceptanceCriteria.text: Streamed assistant deltas render as one growing message, and the stored transcript renders on reopen (component tests with a fake push channel).
Tool calls render collapsed with name, summary and status, and expand to show the result.
While a turn runs the composer is disabled and Stop calls `chats:stop`; afterwards input is enabled again.
Changing the model calls `chats:setModel` and shows a notice, and there is no control to change the agent.
Markdown from the agent cannot inject HTML or scripts (test with a script tag).
Screenshots of an active chat in the running app are attached to the submission.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**.

**In scope**
- Main-pane chat view: header (chat title, agent, model picker, role chip), streaming transcript, composer.
- **Transcript:** user and assistant messages (Markdown rendered safely, with the same renderer as comments and no raw HTML), tool calls as compact collapsible rows (name, summary, status, result), model changes and context resets as inline notices, and errors with their reason.
- **Composer:** multi-line input, Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a newline. While a turn runs the input is disabled and **Stop** is shown.
- **Model picker:** a switch takes effect from the next turn and shows a notice. The agent is shown but cannot be changed.
- Reopening a chat shows its stored transcript at once, then live items as they stream.
- Keep long transcripts responsive: window the list if a 2,000-item chat is slow.

**Verify:** component tests with a fake push channel, and screenshots of the running app.

reasoning.rationale: A streaming chat view with safe Markdown rendering and long-list performance.

tickets.title: Build the chat view: transcript, composer, stop and model switch

acceptanceCriteria.text: A pending request renders the command or edit summary and three buttons, and each button sends its decision through `chats:answerApproval` (component test).
An answered card shows the decision and no longer has buttons.
A chat with a pending request shows a badge in the Agents block and on the collapsed folder row, and the badge clears once answered.

tickets.body:

Size: **medium**.

Exercise the packaged app (`npm run package:win`, `npm run package:mac`) on each OS and record a short report with screenshots. Follow `docs/runbooks/agents.md` as written, and note anywhere it is wrong.

For each agent:
1. Find an existing install. On a machine without it, Download it.
2. Sign in.
3. Create a chat in a tracked folder.
4. Ask it to read a file (no prompt), edit a file (approval: Deny, then Allow once) and run a command (approval).
5. Switch model, and Stop a turn.
6. Quit and reopen the app. Confirm the chat resumes with its context (the agent recalls something from before the restart).
7. Confirm the chat's session appears in Dark Mechanicus with its role and label.
8. Confirm no agent processes are left running after quit.

Then, on a small sample epic: start a run with **Run with an agent** (any one agent) and confirm the orchestrator chat starts the run; start another with **Leave pending** and confirm an external Claude Code session connected as orchestrator picks it up.

Record each defect as a comment on the ticket it belongs to.

reasoning.rationale: Manual and scripted checks of a packaged app on two operating systems with three vendor CLIs.
